title: UDLM Class artifact — the scoped-Class authoring layer
description: Meta-schema for a Class artifact (registry/classes/*.yaml), the authoring layer of the scoped resource-type Class hierarchy (ADR-038). A Class composes SharedDataElements (`$defs.shared_data_element`) at one scope tier — Base (`Category`), Type (`Category.Type`), or Provider (`Category.Type.Provider`) — each `extends` its parent under the Liskov invariant (add or refine, never contradict). Classes become the authoring layer; a generator compiles each Type Class down to the flat resource-type-spec shape consumers read today (`--check`-gated, no downstream break — realization-plan P0). An element's scope position IS its portability (ADR-038 §3), so the realized `portability` block derives from where an instance's populated elements sit rather than being asserted. Part of the UDLM spec, versioned on the SPEC axis. Status: ADR-038 is Proposed pending the engineering pass (#217); this shape inherits that status and executes the decided model (realization-plan).

$id.description: Canonical identifier: https://udlm.dev/registry/udlm/<spec>/class/<ClassName>/<version>. ClassName is the dotted Class name (Compute, Compute.VM, Compute.VM.OCPVirt). A new MAJOR mints a new $id; the uuid never changes (ADR-051).

conforms_to.description: SPEC-axis binding: the UDLM spec major.minor this Class is written against.

uuid.description: Frozen identity (ADR-051): never changes, never reused; a content change bumps `version`, not this.

record_type.description: Dispatch key: this document is a Class artifact (validate.py dispatches it to class.schema.json).

class.description: The scope tier. `base` = Category scope (single-segment name); `type` = Category.Type; `provider` = Category.Type.Provider (provider-authored). MUST match the segment-count of `resource_type`.

resource_type.description: The dotted Class name — one segment for a Base Class (`Compute`), two for a Type Class (`Compute.VM`), three for a Provider Class (`Compute.VM.OCPVirt`). Every element's `scope` MUST equal this.

parent.description: The parent Class this one `extends` (the dotted name one segment shorter). Required for `type` and `provider`; absent for `base` (a Base Class has no parent). The child adds or refines the parent's elements, never contradicts them (the Liskov invariant — enforced by validate_registry's Liskov gate).

version.description: Semver on the CONTENT axis (VERSIONING.md + the ADR-051 publish law). Narrowing an element's scope is breaking even with no shape change (ADR-045/UC-009).

family.description: The entity family this Class belongs to (entities/*.md). The Process family may lead class-system adoption (automation intent, realization-plan priority signal).

status.description: Lifecycle status of the Class definition itself.

adopts.description: External standards this Class adopts by reference (T5) — carried as identity + version-pinned conformance reference, never re-expressed (adopted-standards.md). E.g. a Base Class adopting a schema.org or Redfish shape.

version.description: The pinned standard version the Class conforms to.

binding.description: How this Class binds to it (the join key / conformance reference).

metadata.description: Authoring metadata (author/authority, timestamps, provenance). The provider- or org-authority under which a non-canonical Class is held lives here (ADR-038 authorship & domain).

elements.description: The SharedDataElements this Class contributes at its scope — the composable units (ADR-038 §2). A Type Class's compiled flat spec is its elements plus every ancestor's, landed under `spec.properties`.

then.description: A Base Class has no parent.
A Type/Provider Class MUST name its parent.

shared_data_element.title: SharedDataElement
shared_data_element.description: The composable unit of the Class hierarchy (ADR-038 §2): a data element + its value vocabulary, held at a Class scope. 'Base field', 'shared vocabulary', and 'provider extension' collapse into one shape distinguished only by `scope`. The element `schema` is a declarative JSON-Schema fragment (T1 — data, never executable behavior); `values` are reference-data (ADR-012), the element curated `proposed → canonical`.

element.description: The element name — a lowercase field name in the compiled spec's properties (`cpu`, `memory`, `encryption`). Unique within its owning Class.

scope.description: The Class scope this element is held at, as the dotted Class name. The scope position IS the element's portability (ADR-038 §3) — no separate declaration. MUST equal the owning Class's `resource_type`; the standalone field lets an element be addressed, diffed, and promoted across scopes.

schema.description: The element's declarative shape, a JSON-Schema 2020-12 fragment (the value under the element's key in the compiled spec's `properties`). Declarative constraints only (type/enum/bounds/if-then/pattern) — never executable behavior (T1/T3).

values.description: Optional value vocabulary — reference-data (ADR-012), referenced by handle+version (never inlined enum bodies), so the vocabulary versions independently.

reference.description: Handle of the reference-data record holding the value list.

reference_version.description: Pinned version of the referenced vocabulary (ADR-051).

state.description: Curation state (ADR-038 §2): `proposed` — authored, not yet blessed for portable reliance; `canonical` — curated into the shared library. Promotion (proposed→canonical, or lower scope→higher) is the ADR-038 governed contribution operation, visible in diffs.

optional.description: Whether the element is optional at its scope (ADR-014 optionality-with-conformity).

description.description: Cold-reader prose: what the element models and how a provider naturalizes it (DOC-001).
